title: Operation Clean Heart
subtitle: A military-led anti-crime drive raises enduring questions about security, impunity, and rights.
summary: Operation Clean Heart was a nationwide anti-crime drive launched in October 2002 with military deployment under a civilian government. Rights groups reported arrests, deaths in custody, and later legal immunity for security personnel, while official accounts framed the drive as a law-and-order operation.
heroTagline: A military-led anti-crime drive raises enduring questions about security, impunity, and rights.
whyItMatters: The operation is important for understanding Bangladesh’s later security-state debates, including militarized policing, legal immunity, custodial death allegations, and the normalization of extraordinary law-and-order measures.

historicalDebate: Supporters presented the operation as a response to crime and disorder, while human-rights organizations documented alleged abuses and impunity. Casualty and responsibility claims should be attributed to specific sources.
